Package org.geysermc.paletter

Class Palette

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.Palette
public final class Palette extends Object
Everything a Bedrock client of one version needs to know about items and blocks: vanilla data plus a stack of PaletteLayers, compiled. Immutable and thread safe; share it between all sessions it applies to.

Sending it to a client: 


 palette.applyTo(session.getCodecHelper());     // item and block definitions for the codec
 palette.applyTo(startGamePacket);              // block properties and the block network id mode
 session.sendPacket(palette.voxelShapesPacket());   // always, before start game
 session.sendPacket(palette.itemComponentPacket());
 session.sendPacket(palette.creativeContentPacket());
Translating content uses handles, version independent and interned objects (BedrockBlockState, BedrockItemVariant): block(NbtMap) and item(String, int) find them once, then runtimeId(BedrockBlockState) and blockDefinition(BedrockBlockState) for blocks, resolve(BedrockItemVariant) for items. encode(org.geysermc.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack) and decode(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData) translate whole stacks at the protocol boundary. They are field reads and array lookups that do not allocate. The ids behind the handles are not API.
Since:
0.1.0

    • blockBehaviour

      public @NonNull BlockValues blockBehaviour(int runtimeId)
      The behaviour values (friction, destroy time, collision shape, light, ...) of a block state in this palette: palette.blockBehaviour(runtimeId).get(BlockBehaviour.FRICTION). Vanilla values come from the bundled captures of the palette's version, custom ones from their components. A lookup of the runtime id and an array read; it does not allocate.
      Parameters:
      runtimeId - the runtime id of a state of this palette, as it sends it: the hash, or the sequential id of a palette that numbers them
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the palette has no state with this runtime id; blockDefinition(int) is null then
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • blockOf

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState blockOf(@NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant)
      The block an item variant is sent with in this palette's version, in its default state, as a key: a BedrockBlockState, for every kind of variant (vanilla, extra, custom block items, fallbacks). Paletter alone decides it. A stack may carry a block state of its own, see encode(org.geysermc.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack). blockDefinition(blockOf(variant)) is what is sent, and resolve(variant).block() the same without the key. Unlike Paletter.blockOf(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemVariant), which knows the vanilla variants of the newest data only, this follows the palette: the fallback's block in an old version, the custom block of a layer. runtimeId(BedrockBlockState) gives its runtime id here.
      Returns:
      the block's key, or null if the item is not a block item here (or no state of the newest data resolves to the block, see blockState(BlockDefinition))
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • resolve

      public @Nullable ResolvedItem resolve(@NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant)
      What this palette sends for an item variant, without building an ItemData: the item definition, damage and block of encode(org.geysermc.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack) (fallbacks applied), as one cached record. For the variants of the newest version it is a field read and an array load, it does not allocate. Use it to read the definition or damage of many items; a stack's own block state, count and NBT are not part of it. ResolvedItem.fallback() tells whether the variant is sent as another item, ResolvedItem.variant() which.
      Returns:
      the resolution, or null if the item does not exist in this version and has no fallback
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • blockState

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState blockState(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.BlockDefinition definition)
      The key of a block this palette sends: its exact state, else the first state that resolves to it (several states may share a fallback). For a definition of this palette, blockDefinition(blockState(definition)) is the definition again. The block is looked up by runtime id, the hash of its state: a definition of another palette gives the key of the block with the same runtime id here, as this palette knows it (a custom block of this palette's own layer).
      Returns:
      the key, or null if this palette has no block with the definition's runtime id, no state resolves to it, or the definition is not a RegisteredBlockState
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • encode

      public @NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData encode(@NonNull BedrockItemStack stack)
      Encodes a stack for this palette's version: the item with the aux value, count and NBT, and the block the stack places (its own block state if it has one and the item places blocks, else the item's default block). An item this version does not have, or this palette does not know at all (an identifier nobody registered), is replaced by the same stand-in: the item's fallback, else the default one of the Fallbacks (minecraft:unknown unless configured otherwise), whichever way the item is looked up.
      Returns:
      the item data, or ItemData.AIR only if there is neither a fallback for the item nor a default one (Fallbacks.NONE)
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • decode

      public @Nullable BedrockItemStack decode(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData data)
      Decodes a stack the client sent. The block state is set only if the stack's block differs from the item's default block. The stack of a fallback shared by several variants, or of an item that is not a variant of the newest version, is not recognized.
      Returns:
      the stack, or null for air or an item this palette cannot identify
      Since:

    • sameStack

      public boolean sameStack(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData a, @NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData b)
      Whether two stacks are the same stack of items as far as this palette can tell: the same item definition, damage, count, NBT, canPlace, canBreak, blocking ticks and block. The net id is not part of it.

      Definitions compare by identity, as in Cloudburst (ItemData#equals, which also ignores the block). A definition that is not this palette's own instance (another palette's, or Geyser's own) is first mapped to this palette's entry of the same identifier and runtime id, so a stack of a base palette matches the same stack of a palette extending it. A definition this palette does not have matches only itself. The same goes for block definitions. A missing NBT tag and an empty one are the same, so are missing and empty block lists.

      Stacks that differ only in count, or only in NBT, never match.

      Returns:
      true if the stacks are the same
      Since:
      0.1.0

    • extend

      public @NonNull Palette extend(@NonNull PaletteLayer layer)
      Compiles one more layer on top of this palette, e.g. for one session. Results are cached per layer instance for as long as the layer is referenced.

      Never throws for a problem with the layer's content (a duplicate custom id, a block hash collision, a duplicate item, an exception from a component encoder or a callback): the palette is returned unchanged, with an PaletteReport.Level.ERROR entry in its report() (a copy of this palette's report, which is not modified) naming the layer, the version and the cause. Check PaletteReport.errors().

      Returns:
      the palette with the layer, or this palette (with the error in its report) if the layer failed
